decision: 1:1 cut A: v_1957_24 @ 5.002 s (f150, camera settled after the pull-back; whole front 3/4 + crew powdering) -> full-car scan. cam_A = 12 landmarks, LM solve, then silhouette refine (GrabCut, person masked). f = 18.3 mm on the 20.25 mm portrait sensor, camera height 1.50 m
why: v_2003_40 crops the car in every frame >= 3.2 s. 28 mm (240SX value) gave RMSE 10 px with a visible scale error; the points span 2 m in depth so focal is observable here: free solve 18.3 mm, RMSE 4.7 px, onion shows grille/plate/headlight/mirror/roof aligned. Fixed it at 18.3 mm for the LM + silhouette refine

decision: 1:1 cut B: v_2003_29 last frame 3.501 s (f105, right front fender close-up at the end of the scanner pass) -> scan. cam_B = 6 side landmarks (marker lamp, molding ends, door seam), f = 28 mm, LM solve; hub + seam_bot dropped
why: Camera walks the side continuously (12 px/frame easing to 5), so I solved on the cut frame itself instead of absorbing drift. Side points are near-planar so focal was unobservable (RMSE 4.0-5.7 px for 14-28 mm); the far hood edge only lines up at 28 mm (=240SX iPhone 1x value). Front wheel was dropped because its steer angle may differ from the scan session

decision: Explode = front bumper, rear bumper, 4 wheels cut from the full scan (tools/split_parts.py: bumpers by region at the measured shut lines, wheels are their own mesh islands). Hood left on. No INSIDE claim
why: Rendered every part from behind: bumpers, hood and wheels are exterior skin only (back of the outer surface, mirrored plate). Lifting the hood would open a hole into an unscanned bay
